title: List Story Arcs

items.name: Dan Harmon's Story Circle
items.description: 8-step character transformation circle: Comfort Zone, Need, Unfamiliar Situation, Adapt, Get What They Wanted, Pay a Price, Return, Changed. Ideal for character-driven stories.

items.name: Fichtean Curve
items.description: Plot structure built around sustained, rising tension. Drops readers into conflict via in medias res, escalates through three crises — each more intense than the last — toward a climax, then closes with a short, impactful resolution. Backstory revealed in motion.

items.name: Freytags Pyramid
items.description: Five-Act Structure (Freytag's Pyramid) — Exposition, Rising Action, Climax, Falling Action, Resolution. Creates dedicated space for moral and emotional consequence. Ideal for tragedies, ensemble casts, complex subplots, and character-driven transformation.

items.name: In Medias Res
items.description: Narrative entry technique — opens at a moment of high tension, then reveals backstory gradually through flashback and embedded exposition. Two-layer construction: Entry Scene + Underlying Chronology.

items.name: Kishōtenketsu
items.description: Traditional East Asian four-act narrative framework that builds emotional resonance through contrast and revelation rather than conflict. Four acts: Ki (Introduction), Shō (Development), Ten (Twist/Turn), Ketsu (Conclusion/Resolution). No conflict required.

items.name: Seven-Point Structure
items.description: Dan Wells' Seven-Point Structure — seven pivotal moments built backward from Resolution: Hook, First Plot Point, First Pinch Point, Midpoint, Second Pinch Point, Second Plot Point, Resolution.

items.name: The Hero's Journey
items.description: Joseph Campbell's Monomyth — the most universal narrative framework in human storytelling. 12 stages mapping departure, initiation, and return. The hero leaves the ordinary world, faces trials and transformation through an ordeal, and returns carrying an elixir that benefits others.

items.name: Three-Act Structure
items.description: The most widely used narrative framework in history. Three phases: Setup (25%), Confrontation (50%), Resolution (25%). Key beats: Inciting Incident, Midpoint Shift, Second Plot Point (darkest moment), Climax. Works for every genre.
